findings: acquire.py CANNOT LOAD _provenance.json: the file is {_note, files:[...]}, load_records() expects a flat path-keyed dict. `python3 acquire.py --check` dies with ValueError: _note: missing source_url. Nothing in the pipeline has ever run.
No provenance record carries a destination path field; _note claims 'keyed by destination path' but files is a LIST. The builder must add a `path` per record or re-key the dict.

Only 46 of 211 records carry expected_bytes/expected_sha256 (Codex's Elden Ring set). The other 165 describe images that were in-container; 89 morrowind + 5 anti-generic + 24 hud + 8 rejected files DO still exist on disk, so hashes can be computed locally by make-manifest.py.

Steam apphub homecontent endpoint works for every appid incl. ones with a mod workshop: https://steamcommunity.com/app/<APPID>/homecontent/?userreviewsoffset=0&p=<N>&screenshotspage=<N>&numperpage=50&browsefilter=toprated&appid=<APPID>&appHubSubSection=2&l=english&filterLanguage=default&searchText=<Q>&maxInappropriateScore=100 -- searchText genuinely filters (disjoint id sets per query).

Steam detail page yields File Size / Posted date / WxH in div.detailsStatRight, and the bare https://images.steamusercontent.com/ugc/<a>/<b>/ URL (id=ActualMedia src) is the ORIGINAL bytes -- confirmed 10002569 bytes against a page stating 9.539 MB.
Steam rate-limits hard: 8 concurrent detail fetches returns a ~27.3KB 'Steam Community :: Error' page for ~96% of requests. 3 workers + 0.7s sleep is safe.
